119	### Core Rules
120	
121	Rule ids are `BDY-n`; formulas are `D.n` (Formulas section); acceptance criteria are `AC-BDY-n`; BM1 to BM7 are Body's mutators; `can_*` are its pure precondition reads. Locked constants and formulas from the kernel, the Graph, the Controller, the Pipeline and Layout are used by name with their registry values and are never restated differently (a needed different value would be a CONFLICT line in Open Questions, never a new number): `TICK_RATE` 60, `TILE_PX` 48, `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` 24 (owner: the art bible), `V_WALK` 2, `V_RUN` 3, `V_CARRY` 1 base px per tick, the 1/256 fixed point with its `UNIT` table (256 cardinal, 181 diagonal), `MAX_BODIES` 8, `MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY` 2,000, `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256, `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4, `JOLT_PX` 0. Body-new constants (`FOOT_BOX_W`, `FOOT_BOX_H`, `MAX_ACTORS`, `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT`, `VEL_MAX_PX_PER_TICK`, `DETACH_DRIFT_PX_PER_TICK`, `SWEEP_COST_LOG_MS`) are listed in Tuning Knobs and registered after this GDD is final (Cross-References); any not fixed by a ruling is tagged `[PLACEHOLDER]` (`SWEEP_COST_LOG_MS` is `[PLACEHOLDER]`, suggested 0.05 ms, the per-actor figure of PCI:1078, a logging threshold only). Contracts with undesigned or in-flight systems are marked **(provisional — <system> undesigned)** and name what that GDD must repeat. Conflicts, clarifications and asks are marked **CONFLICT**, **CLARIFY** and **ASK** and are routed in Cross-References and Open Questions, never silently resolved in a neighbour's text. Each rule closes with *Decides:* (the pillar, ruling or sibling rule it serves) and a test tag: (auto) automated, (lint) static check, (review) design review, (spike) engine spike.
122	
123	#### 1.1 Identity, ownership and the no-physics-server rule
124	
125	**BDY-1 — One body per welded set; Body adds pose, not geometry.** A body's identity is Layout's `body_id` (LY-18: Layout allocates it from `next_body_id`, first id 1, and owns `bodies[]`, `section_instances[].body_id`, offsets and `welds[]`). Body stores, per `body_id`, only the frame's POSE (`world_x`, `world_y`), its velocity (`vel_x`, `vel_y`) and the reserved `heading_q`, and, per actor, the actor's body-frame state. Body never allocates, retires or edits a `body_id`, section membership, offset, rectangle, socket, seam or hatch state. The composite welded ship is therefore ONE body in exactly the sense the index means: one frame, one pose row, one rectangle set (`solid_in(body_id, aabb)`), however many sections are welded into it. *Decides:* LY-18, LY-35; P1. (review) grep this GDD for `next_body_id`, `welds[]` and `offset_px` as Body-written fields: zero hits.
126	
127	**BDY-2 — The interior is a pose-invariant integer frame.** Every simulation fact about the interior — a foot box, a `solid_in` rectangle, `pos_curr`, an Emitter anchor, Suit's room lookup, the interior camera pose — is a body-frame integer. **Nothing keyed on a body-frame coordinate reads `world_*` or `vel_*`.** A body that moves in the exterior moves nothing inside it, so the moving-platform problem does not exist as an engine problem; a body in motion and a body at rest produce a byte-identical interior (D.9 states the invariance; the acceptance fixture sets a non-zero `vel` on the avatar's body, runs 600 ticks and compares `canonical_encode(payload["actors"])` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*). Rotation is never a simulation fact (BDY-26). *Decides:* R1, R6, P1, PIPE C2 (PIPE:153). (lint + auto)
128	
129	**BDY-3 — No Godot physics server on any simulation path.** `RigidBody2D`, `CharacterBody2D`, `StaticBody2D`, `AnimatableBody2D`, `PhysicsBody2D`, `Area2D`, `PhysicsServer2D`, `move_and_slide`, `move_and_collide`, `test_move`, `body_test_motion`, engine tile collision and navigation meshes appear in this GDD only in rejected-alternative text and in the lint criterion, which extends the Controller's lint (PCI:900) from the controller, body and presenter directories to the whole Body module and to Layout's (zero matches for that token set; zero matches in the block and the hook for `randi`, `randf`, `randomize`, `Time.`, `OS.get_ticks`, `Engine.get_physics_frames` (the one forbidden-token list for clock, frame-counter and RNG calls is ADR-0010 SIM-02, section 4.5; ADR-0001 and ADR-0005 point at it), float-typed declarations and non-integer `Vector2(`; no script under `src/sim/body/` names `Node2D`, `Camera2D` or `Viewport`; the PROJECTOR lives in `src/presentation/projector/`, ADR-0010 section 1.2) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0010 sync)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **The token grep is not sufficient on its own, because GDScript type inference can silently produce a float** (`var x := a / b` on ints is integer division, but `var y := a * 0.5` or an untyped `Variant` path is a float that no token list names). The lint therefore also **promotes the GDScript typing warnings to errors for every script under the Body and Layout directories (ADR-0010 section 5 widens this to all of `src/` and `tools/`)** — `UNTYPED_DECLARATION`, `INFERRED_DECLARATION`, `UNSAFE_*`, `NARROWING_CONVERSION`, `INTEGER_DIVISION`, `INFERENCE_ON_VARIANT` — and CI fails on any warning raised by a file in those directories (`debug/gdscript/warnings/directory_rules` exists on 4.7.2 with include/exclude decisions and one global severity per warning (probed 2026-10-28); ADR-0010 section 5 promotes every warning to an error for all of `src/` and `tools/`, which subsumes the Body and Layout directories, and the CI gate is that every script loads) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0010 sync)*. `INTEGER_DIVISION` makes every `/` on integers an error unless annotated, which leaves exactly ONE annotated `/` site in `src/`, inside `IntMath.trunc_div` (`src/shared/int_math.gd`; `floor_div` calls it, BDY-35; ADR-0010 SIM-05, PRJ-04). The 2D server that exists is Godot Physics 2D (**verified-from-docs**: `modules/physics.md`, "2D physics UNCHANGED (still Godot Physics 2D)"; Jolt is the 3D default since 4.6 and does not apply to 2D). Body relies on it for nothing; the one candidate use is presentation-only debris at Vertical Slice, excluded from `ALL_SIM` (ADR-BODY-05). *Rejected alternatives:* one `RigidBody2D` or `CharacterBody2D` per ship with engine collision shapes built from Layout (contradicts four designed GDDs, makes G3 depend on a recorded physics replay, adds an unmeasured shape rebuild per weld and per cut, and lets rotation leak inside, PIPE C2); an engine-physics exterior hybrid (a second authority for pose). *Decides:* R1, R13, KRN:123 (G3), Guard rail 3. (lint) → ADR-BODY-01, ADR-BODY-05.
130	
131	**BDY-4 — Who is an actor; what is not.** An `actors` row has `kind SEAT | AGENT`. MVP rows are `SEAT` only: one per bound player seat. **A horror holds its own position**: of the two paths (keep a position in its own state block and call the pure `LocomotionStep` of BDY-10, or register `AGENT` rows here), Horror Entities chose path 1 (HE-23: position, residue and `last_octant` in `horror.state`, movement only through `LocomotionStep` with Body's foot box; consistency pass 2026-10-27), so MVP `AGENT` rows stay unused, and a horror's footprint is a Graph trail, never a Body fact. **No prop is an actor**: loose items are Interaction records in section-local pixels (IA-28, LY-22: "a weld or a detach moves nothing"); static props and machinery are Layout rectangles; a thrown glowstick lands analytically (IA-29). A Vertical Slice movable prop adds one `kind` here and one bump-list entry in Layout (LY:229) deliberately. **Orphaned bodies persist**: a body left with no actor keeps its pose row; membership and discard are Layout's, Assembly's and Web Map's (`discard_section_geometry`); Body offers `actors_on(body_id)` and `body_count()` for their decisions. Filter-only phantoms (hallucination class (a)) have no Body row. *Decides:* R9, R18, R19; P4. (review)
132	
133	#### 1.2 The block
134	
135	**BDY-5 — `body.state` is one SHARED `SIM` block.** Registration (CR-8, with `supported_versions` from SL-15 item 2, SL:224): `block_id body.state`; owner Ship Body; `class SIM`; `persist true`; `persist_scope WORLD`; `scope SHARED`; `repl_hint SHARED_SUMMARY`; `schema_version 1`; `supported_versions [1]`; `restore_after: [layout.state]`; exactly one hook, `body.integrate`; exactly one `PROJECTOR` subscriber, `body.projector`. Two sparse tables: `bodies` keyed by `body_id` (Layout's id) and `actors` keyed by `actor_id`, plus the block-local counter `next_actor_id` (CR-8: entity ids are allocated by the owning block from a counter stored inside it). Body repeats what Layout asked it to repeat (LY-18): it owns `body.state` (pose, velocity, actor positions); its `restore_after` is `[layout.state]`; and it owns the physics `PROJECTOR` slot (BDY-33). *Rejected:* `PER_PLAYER` scope (bodies and pods have no PlayerId); two blocks (`body.state` and `body.frames`) — a second restore node and a second owner registration where EM-1 names one. *Decides:* R2, EM-1, SL:288; CR-8. (auto: registration lint) → ADR-BODY-02.
136	
137	**BDY-6 — One position name.** The persisted canonical field is **`pos_curr`** (the name EM:426, LO:217 and SL:474 already read). `pos_prev` is DERIVED: set `:= pos_curr` in Body's own `post_restore`, at placement and at every transfer, never persisted *(Amended 2026-10-29 — sync knock-on fix: the `post_restore` reset is a Body-internal derivation of a non-persisted field, not the camera-continuity mechanism, which is solely the kernel `snap_baseline` plus the camera CUT on a `load_seq` change, ADR-0008 § 6.1; see BDY-31)*. The Controller's `pos` (PCI:447, "`body.state.pos`") is an alias for `pos_curr`; this sentence is where the alias is declared, once (a wording note is routed to Save/Load, whose SL:474 and SL:849 list both `pos` and `pos_curr`, and to the Controller). `blocked` and every `diag` value are derived and outside the hashed set. *Decides:* R2, R3, PIPE C5, SL-15 item 8 (SL:230). (auto)
138	
139	**BDY-7 — Persisted fields (schema v1).** Per actor: `{actor_id, kind, seat, body_id, pos_curr (x, y), sub (x, y), last_octant, odometer}`. Per body, sparse (a row absent means all zeros): `{body_id, world_x, world_y, vel_x, vel_y, heading_q}`. Block scalar: `next_actor_id`. `last_octant` (0-7, 8 = NONE) is **Body's own** record of the octant its last step integrated; it is a different field from `controller.state`'s decel-ladder memory of the same name (PCI:311), and this sentence is the disambiguation. `seat` is the PlayerId whose `controller.state` row feeds this actor's intent; **seat 0 means "no seat" (`AGENT` rows; any number of `AGENT` rows may carry it) and PlayerIds start at 1; two `SEAT` rows may never share a seat, and a `SEAT` row with `seat` 0 or a negative seat is `BDY_PLACE_BAD_KIND` at placement and `BDY_RESTORE_KIND` on restore** (the kernel defines a PlayerId as "a stable seat identity (1 in single-player)", KRN:52, and Suit keys by an integer PlayerId, SE-2; no designed GDD assigns PlayerId 0, and the kernel states the reservation once, KRN:52, answered *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*); it is persisted because the kernel's binding table "is not saved, since sessions rebuild it" (KRN:100), so after a restore nothing else says which `actor_id` is seat 1; Body matches an actor to its Controller row on its own `seat` field, so no kernel reverse lookup is needed. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Who rebuilds the kernel's `PlayerId → {controlled entity IDs}` binding after a load (the step KRN:100 left unowned until 2026-10-28; ANSWERED, below).** KRN:100 says the table "may be rebuilt from Body's `seat` field" and SL-20 says "a session rebuilds it", but at the design review no GDD assigned the step, and the MVP death-restart path (restore the last autosave, then play) needs it: without it a seat-1 command fails the authority stage (`ACTOR_NOT_OWNED`, KRN CR-5) after every restore. Body's half of the contract is stated here and is closed: Body publishes the pure read `seat_bindings() -> [(seat, actor_id)]` (ascending `seat`, `SEAT` rows only, derived from the actors table on each call, no persisted field) and nothing else. The other half is the kernel's *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6)*: kernel CR-7 rebuilds `PlayerId -> {controlled entity IDs}` as the last step of every `LOADING` (after the last `post_restore()`, before `RUNNING`), calling Body's registered binding source `seat_bindings()` and binding each pair (KRN-BIND-01). Body registers `seat_bindings` as a binding source at BOOTING and does nothing else. **ANSWERED 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling G6): kernel CR-7 rebuild, KRN-BIND-01 to 04; Save/Load SL-20, AC-SL-149.** AC-BDY-6 and AC-BDY-138 are Body's explicit INTEGRATION CLOSURE GATE: they run against the real kernel and the real Save/Load registrations in the composition-root story (the first end-to-end tick story), and Body's epic does not close until both pass. A `SEAT` row with no Controller row (a Vertical Slice disconnect, a corrupt save) is **not stepped**, is treated as `v_eff` 0 (`sub` and `last_octant` reset) and is counted `BDY_SEAT_UNBOUND`. `odometer` is 64-bit and travels in the binary payload (SL-2) as a native int64 (exact); the halves-or-strings convention remains legal, and is mandatory only where a value can reach JSON (header, dump-save), never as a JSON number *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0006 sync)*. *(orchestrator ruling: `seat` is an additive field beyond R3's list, adopted from the technical-director and engine-programmer proposals, which independently found the gap; the engine-programmer's name `owner_ref` is dropped in favour of the kernel's vocabulary, CR-7.)* *Decides:* R2, R3, CR-7, CR-8. (auto)
140	
141	#### 1.3 The tick
142	
143	**BDY-8 — `body.integrate` registration and order.** `hook_id body.integrate`, owner Ship Body, divisor 1, offset 0, **`after: [controller.step, layout.doors]`**. This resolves Layout Open Question 6 and LY-10 (LY:217-218) inside Body's own registration: an opening `area` or `door_state` changes only in P2; `layout.doors` runs in P3 and writes the leaf rectangle set; `body.integrate` reads that set in the same tick. The order is a PARTIAL order, not a chain: `body.integrate` runs after both `controller.step` and `layout.doors`, which are mutually unordered (`layout.doors` is `after: []` and must not depend on `body.integrate`); `controller.step` follows `suit.vitals` (SE-1, SE:146; PCI:133, PCI:145); `emitter.place` is `after: [body.integrate, graph.propagate.failure]` (EM:104, transitive, no Emitter edit). Every hook id this GDD writes is one its owner registers; the ids Body names are `suit.vitals`, `controller.step`, `layout.doors`, `body.integrate`, `emitter.place`, `graph.propagate.power`, `graph.propagate.atmo` and `graph.propagate.failure` (others, such as Interaction's `interaction.step`, IA:428, are registered and are simply not named here), written exactly because an unknown id fails boot (CR-3). The Controller's PC-14 and PC-15 text "`after: controller.step`" is a wording refresh (routed), not a contract change. *Decides:* R4, LY-10, CR-3, reflexion pattern 6. (auto: topological-order test)

Its SIM-readable sibling is the derived read `moved(actor_id) := pos_curr - pos_prev` (CP-3; States 3.6): it adds no persisted field and is readable by a SIM hook only if that hook is ordered `after: [body.integrate]` (lint). `PC_BLOCKED_TICKS` is the Controller's counter and is cited, not re-registered. *Decides:* R16, PCI:491, PCI:502. The preconditions are pure reads the caller's `validate` invokes (BDY-21): `BDY_PLACE_UNKNOWN_BODY`, `BDY_PLACE_INSIDE_FOOTPRINT` (the foot box at `pos` intersects a SOLID rectangle), `BDY_PLACE_CAPACITY` (`actor_count >= MAX_ACTORS`), `BDY_PLACE_BAD_KIND`, `BDY_PLACE_DUPLICATE_SEAT`. `MAX_ACTORS` 8 (range 4-16) `[PLACEHOLDER]`, Body-registered: four seats at Vertical Slice plus horrors. 181	**BDY-21 — Mutator surface BM1-BM7, all Class A; every mutator returns OK or a FAULT_CODE; validation is a pure read.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the contract of this rule is rewritten; the earlier assumption that an apply cannot fail is struck, because it contradicted MSA-14, MSA-31 and AC-MSA-142)* Body publishes seven mutators — BM1 `place_actor`, BM2 `remove_actor`, BM3 `rebase_on_attach`, BM4 `rebase_on_detach` (five arguments, the fifth `cap_rects[]`, BDY-24 (iii) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6)*), BM5 `transfer_actor`, BM6 `set_body_velocity`, BM7 `set_body_pose` (added at the consistency pass 2026-10-27, routed from `web-map-and-transit.md` ASK-B1, WM-6) — each called only from Assembly's or Transit's single `apply`, AFTER the Layout mutator in the same `WriteScope` (KRN:197 names the three mutator owners; the order inside one scope, Graph then Layout then Body, is Assembly's contract (Modular Ship Assembly is Designed and repeats it: MSA-14, table T3 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*), implied by Layout returning the records Body consumes, LY-16, LY-17). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Every mutator returns a status; none is assumed to succeed.** GDScript has no throw and no catch, and `assert()` is compiled out of a release export, so a mutator that cannot honour its apply-time predicate has to say so in its return value (the caller's half is MSA-31, MSA-14 and AC-MSA-142). BM2 to BM7 return an `int`: `OK` (0) or a NEGATIVE `FAULT_CODE`, which is the negated Body reason constant of the `can_*` read that would have rejected the call (reason constants are positive ints, so `-BDY_PLACE_CAPACITY` is a `FAULT_CODE`). BM1 returns the allocated `actor_id` (an int >= 1) or a negative `FAULT_CODE`: one return channel, no out-parameter and no per-call allocation. `rc < 0` is a fault for every mutator. The caller's `apply` (Assembly's or Transit's) checks the status after EVERY Body call and, on the first negative value, calls the kernel's fault entry (MSA-31, ASK K2) and makes no further mutator call, so a failure inside `apply` moves the kernel to `FAULTED` (KRN:104). Body's mutators are not kernel-registered owner callables (they run inside the caller's `apply`); Body's kernel-registered callables (`body.integrate`, `snapshot`, `restore`, `post_restore`) take the kernel's `ctx`, return their results through it and end `return ctx.complete()` (delegated ruling R3). What R8 calls "BM1 validates ..." is **published as pure `can_*` precondition reads** — `can_place`, `can_remove`, `can_rebase_attach`, `can_rebase_detach`, `can_transfer`, `can_set_velocity`, `can_set_pose` — that the caller's `validate` invokes before any mutator runs, exactly as the Graph's pure `can_join` serves weld validation; inside `apply` the same checks are re-evaluated as the apply-time predicate below, and every mutator is **check-then-write** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: it evaluates its WHOLE predicate before its first row write, so a call that returns a `FAULT_CODE` has written nothing (the tables, `next_actor_id`, the dirty set and the event queue are exactly as before the call, and no half-applied weld or cut exists). Every apply-time defect calls the injectable **`plan_mismatch_sink`**, a module-level `Callable` taking `(mutator_id, code)`: its default increments the counter `BDY_PLAN_MISMATCH`, which is ACTIVE in every build, and in a debug build also calls `push_error`. No mutator path uses `assert()`, because a GDScript `assert` is compiled out of release and cannot be intercepted by a test; a test injects a recording sink and exercises every defect in the ordinary debug gdUnit4 runner (harness rule 1). The apply-time predicate per mutator is a mismatch with the pre-state its `can_*` read would have proven: BM1 any `can_place` reason; BM2 an unknown actor; BM3 the two ids equal or the surviving body not live in Layout; BM4 the old body not live, `new_body_id` not live in Layout, or a `moved_sections[]` member not owned by `new_body_id` (the call-order trap of BDY-23), an actor of the old body overlapping `cap_rects[]` (`actors_overlapping(old_body_id, cap_rects)` non-empty, BDY-24 (iii)) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6)*, or *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* a new pose row out of range *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: this one is NOT a failing predicate; it is the saturate-and-continue branch of the split below)*; BM5 an unknown actor, an unknown destination or an arrival box inside a SOLID rectangle; BM6 an unknown body or a velocity out of range; BM7 an unknown body or a coordinate out of range. **The split per defect class *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.** (i) *Return-the-code class* (the call writes nothing and returns the `FAULT_CODE`; the caller faults the kernel): an unknown, equal or dead id (BM2 `BDY_UNKNOWN_ACTOR`; BM3 and BM4 `BDY_REBASE_SAME_BODY` or `BDY_REBASE_UNKNOWN_BODY`; BM5 `BDY_UNKNOWN_ACTOR` or `BDY_PLACE_UNKNOWN_BODY`; BM6 `BDY_VEL_UNKNOWN_BODY`; BM7 `BDY_POSE_UNKNOWN_BODY`); a BM4 `moved_sections[]` member not owned by `new_body_id` (`BDY_REBASE_SECTION_NOT_OWNED`, the call-order trap of BDY-23); *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6)* a BM4 call for which `actors_overlapping(old_body_id, cap_rects)` is non-empty (`BDY_REBASE_ACTOR_IN_CAP`, BDY-24 (iii); evaluated before the first write, so the call writes nothing); a BM3 or BM4 `frame_shift_px` off Layout's 24-px grid (`BDY_REBASE_SHIFT_OFF_GRID`); any rejected BM1, including an over-cap one (`BDY_PLACE_CAPACITY` and the other `can_place` reasons); a BM5 arrival box inside a SOLID rectangle (`BDY_PLACE_INSIDE_FOOTPRINT`); a BM6 velocity or BM7 coordinate out of range (`BDY_VEL_OUT_OF_RANGE`, `BDY_POSE_OUT_OF_RANGE`; the call writes nothing, so no unloadable row can result). (ii) *Saturate-and-continue class* (the call completes and returns `OK`): **only BM4's new pose row**, where `world_old + frame_shift_px` leaves `±WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` or `vel_old` plus drift leaves `±VEL_MAX_PX_PER_TICK`; it saturates per BDY-23, the sink counts `BDY_WORLD_LIMIT` (where applicable) and `BDY_PLAN_MISMATCH`, and BM4 returns `OK`. The reason is the user's ruling that a death restarts from the last autosave: by the time BM4 runs the Graph and Layout have already applied the cut, and a row `restore` would reject (`BDY_RESTORE_POSE_RANGE`) would make the next autosave unloadable, so this branch is load-bearing and must not become a fault. Class (i) is checked first: a BM4 call that has both an unknown new body and a range overflow returns the code. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6)* Within class (i) the id, ownership and grid defects are checked before the cap overlap (the overlap read needs a live old body), and `can_rebase_detach(old_body_id, frame_shift_px)` is unchanged by the cap guard (it takes no `cap_rects`), so Assembly's V4 and the MSA-7 reason order are untouched. *Consistency* after any call, including every call that returned a `FAULT_CODE`: `restore(snapshot())` accepts the block, actor ids are unique and below `next_actor_id`, and every `body_id` in either table is live in Layout; there is no exception (an over-cap BM1 is a returned code and writes no row, so no over-cap row can exist and Open Question 13 is closed). This *is* validate-then-apply (CR-9) with the two halves held by different owners. None of the `can_*` reads needs Layout's apply-time return record *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: except that `can_rebase_detach` takes the seam's `frame_shift_px` as a caller-supplied argument, below, exactly as `docked` does)*: each proves only that the bodies it names are live in Layout's pre-state, that ids differ and, for BM4, that the new pose row is in range (`can_rebase_detach(old_body_id, frame_shift_px)` proves that the old body is live in Layout *and, (Amended 2026-10-27 — design review), that the cut cannot produce a pose row `restore` would reject*: it answers `BDY_REBASE_POSE_OUT_OF_RANGE` when `world_old + frame_shift_px` leaves `±WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` on either axis and `BDY_VEL_OUT_OF_RANGE` when `vel_old` plus the drift (BDY-28) leaves `±VEL_MAX_PX_PER_TICK`; `frame_shift_px` is the value Layout's D.12 fixes for the seam (Assembly passes its own V3 `frame_shift_px`, the value its `detach_preview` produced, to this read, so the range guard runs on the real validate path; the Layout preview itself is optional, Open Question 34; Assembly's V4 row and AC-MSA-77 still show the one-argument form, which Assembly conforms to this signature because the registry's `body_mutators` is sourced here (G1); at apply time Layout's REAL record is authoritative as for every other mutator) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; a fresh Layout `body_id` cannot already own a Body row, because `BDY_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_BODY` rejects any Body id Layout does not hold, and an apply-time disagreement between a returned record and the pre-state returns its `FAULT_CODE` and is reported to the sink as `BDY_PLAN_MISMATCH`); at `apply` time Assembly passes Layout's REAL record, which Body treats as authoritative. Body registers no player command type and subscribes to no Layout dirty keys. *Rejected:* Body reconciling from Layout's dirty keys inside its hook (a write outside a mutator; CR-9), and Layout calling Body (breaks the acyclic LY-18). Dirty keys use Layout's encoding `(KIND << 32) | id`, `BODY` 2 (the shared family) and a new `ACT` 4, with **explicit dirty marking in every mutator** (4.7 packed-array element writes no longer call the property setter — verified-from-docs, `breaking-changes.md` 4.6 to 4.7, "Packed array element writes"). The full interface is in States and Transitions. *Decides:* R8, CR-9, LY-18; P1 (no half-applied weld leaves an actor in a frame that does not exist). (auto) → ADR-BODY-02.

183	**BDY-22 — Weld transfer (BM3).** On attach, only actors on the ABSORBED body are touched: `pos_curr += frame_shift_px`, `body_id := surviving_body_id`, `pos_prev := pos_curr`, `sub` and `last_octant` untouched (a whole-pixel shift cannot disturb a residue), and `BODY_TRANSFER{weld}` is emitted for those actors only. **Host-body actors are untouched** ("a weld moves nothing already built", LY:250). BM3 deletes the absorbed body's pose row. The mutator runs in P2 and `body.integrate` in P3 of the same tick, so the shifted actor is stepped this tick from the shifted position with a zero interpolation delta; the one-tick transfer artefact is removed by the Pipeline's C5 REBASE, not by Body: `BODY_TRANSFER{weld}` carries `frame_delta_px = +frame_shift_px` (3.7), and the Pipeline shifts its camera solver's `f` and history by it into the surviving body's frame and keeps the lag, so the avatar's screen position does not move (registry `camera_cut_predicates`: a weld or detach `BODY_TRANSFER` that carries `frame_delta_px` is a rebase, not a cut); a hard cut, never a pan, happens only where the new body's camera bounds clamp the rebased target *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. `frame_shift_px` is Layout's return value (the absorbed frame's origin expressed in the host frame, LY D.6; airlock fixture `(576, 96)`); Assembly passes the home-ship socket first, so the home-ship's body survives (LY-16, LY OQ-21). The invariant that makes this safe, stated as a test: for every actor moved, `(actor_section, actor_local_px)` is identical before and after (BDY-29). *Decides:* R7, LY-16; T3. (auto: D.4 fixture)
184	
185	**BDY-23 — Detach transfer (BM4): the foot origin picks the side.** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6)* Before any row is written BM4 evaluates its whole apply-time predicate, including the cap guard of BDY-24 (iii): if `actors_overlapping(old_body_id, cap_rects)` is non-empty it writes nothing and returns `-BDY_REBASE_ACTOR_IN_CAP`. A box that straddles the seam overlaps the seam's hatch rectangles, so in play it is refused rather than split; the side rule below is the specification for every origin that passes the guard and the unit-test surface with `cap_rects[]` empty. For each actor on the old body the side is the component whose section contains the foot ORIGIN on the detach tick (PCI:651, PCI:1001); a foot box straddling the seam is not split. Because BM4 runs after Layout's mutator, Layout has already re-based the moved sections, so Body evaluates containment against the **reconstructed pre-cut geometry**: for `s` in `moved_sections[]`, `offset_pre(s) = section_offset(s) + frame_shift_px`; for every other section of the old body `offset_pre(s) = section_offset(s)` (D.5; stated once as the call-order trap). Containment is by the section's FLOOR area (its rooms and the rectangles it owns, including its own 24-px hull footprint and hatch rectangles), never by bounding box, because hull-abutting sections have overlapping bounding boxes. Actors on `C_new`: `pos_curr -= frame_shift_px`, `body_id := new_body_id`, `pos_prev := pos_curr`, `sub := (0, 0)`, `last_octant` kept (harmless: `sub` is already zero, so a held key reads "no change"); emit `BODY_TRANSFER{detach}` with `frame_delta_px = -frame_shift_px` (3.7) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Actors on `C_keep` are untouched. An origin lying in no section (an exterior gap, a defect) stays on `C_keep` and counts `BDY_TRANSFER_NO_SECTION`; this is a defect-only state, CI asserts it never occurs in a clean build (AC-BDY-29a), and its consequence is exterior exposure, never the last room's atmosphere (BDY-29, 8.3). BM4 creates the new body's pose row from the old body's (`world := world_old + frame_shift_px`, `vel := vel_old`, plus the default-zero detach drift of BDY-28), so a cut leaves both halves co-moving; *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **the new row is always restorable.** The pose range is a restore rule (`BDY_RESTORE_POSE_RANGE`), so a BM4 that wrote an out-of-range row would make the next autosave unloadable and break BDY-21's `restore(snapshot())` guarantee and the death-restart path. The normal defence is `can_rebase_detach`'s `BDY_REBASE_POSE_OUT_OF_RANGE` and `BDY_VEL_OUT_OF_RANGE` (BDY-21) and Transit's re-origin discipline (WM-6 keeps every pose within `WEB_COORD_BUDGET_PX`, 1/32 of the limit). The apply-time net for a caller that ignored the read is the D.7 freeze rule applied to the new row: if `world_old + frame_shift_px` leaves the range the new `world` is saturated per axis to `±WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` and `vel` is set to `(0, 0)`; if `vel_old + drift` leaves `±VEL_MAX_PX_PER_TICK` it is saturated per axis; `BDY_WORLD_LIMIT` (where applicable) and `BDY_PLAN_MISMATCH` count through the sink and BM4 returns `OK`: this is the saturate-and-continue class of BDY-21, and every other BM4 defect returns its `FAULT_CODE` and writes nothing *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. This is the one place a stored coordinate is saturated, it is defect-only, it touches the exterior pose alone (the interior bytes are unchanged, BDY-2), and the exterior `abs` conservation below is waived on that branch; the Controller clears `channel_ref` and keeps `octant`, `carry_ref` and `facing` (its rule, cited). The `sub` zeroing is a TRANSFER rule and does not conflict with BDY-31 (a restore is not a transfer). **Conservation law (the spike's falsifiable invariant):** with `abs(actor) = world(body_of(actor)) + pos_curr(actor)`, detach conserves `abs` exactly for every actor on either side; a weld conserves `abs` iff the docking invariant of BDY-27 holds; and **a weld followed by a cut of the same seam is not in general an identity on `pos_curr`** (detach re-bases to the section `m` with minimum id in `C_new`, LY D.12, while a weld shifts by the absorbed offset; the two coincide only when the absorbed body's section sat at its own frame origin), so any round-trip criterion asserts `abs` and the section-local position, never raw `pos_curr`. Fixture: Layout `fixture_chain` (chain 1 `(0, 0)`, 3 `(576, 96)`, 4 `(1056, 96)` cut at the (1, 3) seam: `frame_shift_px (576, 96)`, new offsets 3 `(0, 0)`, 4 `(480, 0)`). *Decides:* R7, LY-17, PCI:651; T3. (auto: D.5 fixture)

187	**BDY-24 — The hatch-cap hazard: refuse on player origin, never displace.** After a cut the socket's hatch is a SOLID `HULL` rectangle (`CAPPED` or `CUT_OPEN`, LY-15), so an actor standing in the hatch passage ends inside a footprint — a real hazard no designed GDD names. (i) Body publishes the pure read `actors_overlapping(body_id, rects[]) -> actor_id[]` (ascending); Assembly's `validate` of a PLAYER-origin cut rejects while it is non-empty for the seam's two hatch rectangles (the reason code is Assembly's: `MSA.CUT_BLOCKED`, adopted in MSA-21). **Origin is read as Assembly's `cause`** (consistency pass 2026-10-27, routed from `modular-ship-assembly.md` C7): hooks submit SYSTEM-origin commands only (KRN CR-3), so every channel-completed cut reaches P2 as SYSTEM-origin; throughout this GDD "PLAYER-origin cut" means `seam_cut {cause CHANNEL}` (rejects, at begin, handoff and completion) and "SYSTEM-origin cut" means `seam_cut {cause CASCADE}` (defers, MSA-22). (ii) If any transfer nonetheless lands an actor's foot box inside a SOLID rectangle — a restore of an older save, a template defect (a cut can no longer be the cause, clause (iii)) — BDY-16 applies: the body is never displaced. PCI:650 already rules the door analogue (a system-origin close enters `CLOSING_BLOCKED` and retries); this GDD turns the mirror into a **named must-repeat for Modular Ship Assembly (now Designed and repeating it, MSA-21, MSA-22; recorded in 8.3) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: was "provisional, undesigned")***: a SYSTEM-origin cut DEFERS while `actors_overlapping` is non-empty for the seam's two hatch rectangles, and the cut is preceded by the Pillar 2 tell window that Assembly and Adaptive Audio own (the 10 to 30 s escalating tell; the Graph's `W_MIN_WARNING_S` fairness gate), so a breach-driven cut can never separate a crewmate or seal one into a cap without a telegraphed window. How long a deferred cut may wait is Assembly's (Open Question 10); on expiry the cut is abandoned, never forced (MSA-22); Body supplies the pure read and, behind Assembly's V5, the apply-time net of clause (iii). The no-displacement rule is unchanged and correct: the deferral prevents the overlap, it does not resolve one. (iii) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6)* **Crisis-cut guard — Resolved 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6 (user delegated all remaining calls): there is no cut path around Assembly's completion validate V5** — every cut is `seam_cut {cause CHANNEL|CASCADE}`, CHANNEL rejects (`MSA.CUT_BLOCKED`), CASCADE defers and on expiry is abandoned, never forced (MSA-21, MSA-22), and Layout's `detach_section` has no other caller; Layout's "crisis cut" is the CASCADE cut. Body rules REFUSE, not EJECT (ejection is the displacement that P2 and PCI:650 struck). Body adds the apply-time net behind V5: BM4 becomes `rebase_on_detach(old_body_id, new_body_id, moved_sections[], frame_shift_px, cap_rects[])`, where `cap_rects[]` is the `rects[]` of Layout's `detach_section` record (the seam's hatch rectangles, pre-cut body frame, equal to `detach_preview().rects[]`). Its apply-time predicate, evaluated before the first write (check-then-write), gains a class-(i) member: if `actors_overlapping(old_body_id, cap_rects)` is non-empty BM4 writes nothing and returns `-BDY_REBASE_ACTOR_IN_CAP`; the caller faults the kernel (MSA-31) and `BDY_PLAN_MISMATCH` counts through the sink. `can_rebase_detach(old_body_id, frame_shift_px)` is unchanged, so Assembly's V4 and the MSA-7 reason order are untouched. `BDY_REBASE_ACTOR_IN_CAP` reads 0 in every clean build (a CI gate alongside `PC_FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP` and `BDY_TRAPPED_ACTOR`). Consequence: a cut can no longer create the cap trap; its only sources are a restore of an older save and a template defect (BDY-16). **Struck:** a defensive deterministic push-out and its diagnostic, which contradict PCI:650 and P2. *Decides:* R7, LY-11, PCI:650, P2. (auto: hatch-cap fixture)

189	**BDY-25 — The pod hop is a body transfer.** BM5 `transfer_actor(actor_id, to_body_id, pos, cause POD)`: `pos_prev := pos_curr`, `sub := (0, 0)`, `last_octant` kept, `carry_ref` kept (the Controller's, PCI:694); emit `BODY_TRANSFER{pod}`. Body does not search for a free arrival cell (that would be a displacement): `can_transfer` answers `BDY_PLACE_INSIDE_FOOTPRINT` to the caller and Transit owns the alternative cell; two crewmates arriving at one cell is legal (BDY-17). **The pod is a Layout body** (Web Map & Transit is Designed and repeats it, WM-5 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: was "provisional — Web Map & Transit undesigned")*; Derelict Authoring DA-3 authors the `pod` template, one room `pod_cabin`, seat cell (72, 48)): a section built by Layout `build_section` from a pod template, with its own Layout `body_id`, counted against `MAX_BODIES`; Body places the actor on it. Uniform rectangle and occluder paths and the Emitter's `body_id` partition (EM-30) and Lighting's mask bits then work unchanged. Web Map & Transit must repeat (DA-3 already does): the pod template exists and the pod is a body. **Web Map's answer to SE-35 (consistency pass 2026-10-27; WM-5, WM-17):** `room_at` answers `pod_cabin`, never NONE, on the pod (consistent with BDY-29: NONE is never a place on a Layout body); the pod's air is Suit's `HOLD_ROOM` keyed on `loco_state == IN_POD` (WM-17, Web Map ASK-S1), not a NONE answer. *Decides:* R15, PCI:173, PCI:192, PCI:694, EM-30. (auto)

191	#### 1.5 Pose in the exterior frame, the inertial interior
192	
193	**BDY-26 — World pose, velocity and range.** `world_x`, `world_y` are integer base px that locate **the body-frame origin** (Layout's frame origin for that `body_id`, LY-3 (b)) in the exterior frame; `vel_x`, `vel_y` are whole base px per tick (no sub-pixel exterior residue in schema v1: the exterior layer is presentation and may interpolate by `tick_alpha`; a slower drift would be a schema bump made deliberately). `body.integrate` adds `vel` to `world` once per tick before stepping actors (BDY-9). Ranges: `|world_*| <= WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` 2^22 and `|vel_*| <= VEL_MAX_PX_PER_TICK` 16, both Body-registered `[PLACEHOLDER]`; `can_set_velocity` rejects `BDY_VEL_UNKNOWN_BODY` and `BDY_VEL_OUT_OF_RANGE`; the defence against a leg that would run past the world range is the `BDY_WORLD_LIMIT` freeze of BDY-9 (a mis-scripted leg is Transit's lint, not a Body projection); the 2^22 bound exists so a canvas offset (a difference of two world coordinates, within ±2^23) stays inside the range a float32 `Node2D.position` represents exactly (2^24) **[UNV: build precision]** (→ ADR-BODY-03). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Lowering either bound is a schema bump.** `BDY_RESTORE_POSE_RANGE` rejects any saved row beyond the CURRENT `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` or `VEL_MAX_PX_PER_TICK`, so lowering either constant after saves exist makes those saves unloadable; a lowering therefore ships with `schema_version` 2 and a migration that saturates the stored rows (Save/Load's migration, SL), never as a silent tuning change. 207	**BDY-32 — Determinism contract (G3 and G4).** (1) *Order:* actors in ascending `actor_id`, bodies in ascending `body_id`, pose before actors; actors cannot affect one another (BDY-17), so actor order cannot change a result, yet it is fixed so that diagnostics and dirty-key insertion are reproducible. (2) *Sweep input:* Layout's result arrives in key order `(section_id, idx)`; the sweep takes a minimum over candidates and is order-independent by construction, and the order is asserted in debug so a Layout reorder is caught. (3) *Canonical bytes* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: canonical bytes are the kernel's (D.12 TLV), not Body's. Body defines only the SHAPE of the `snapshot()` payload: a Dictionary with exactly five keys `next_actor_id` (int), `n_bodies` (int), `n_actors` (int), `bodies` (Array of ints, `n_bodies * 6`, rows ascending by `body_id`: `body_id, world_x, world_y, vel_x, vel_y, heading_q`) and `actors` (Array of ints, `n_actors * 10`, rows ascending by `actor_id`: `actor_id, kind, seat, body_id, pos_x, pos_y, sub_x, sub_y, last_octant, odometer`); plain `Array`, never Packed, never floats, no `pos_prev`. Body ships no byte writer and does not use `var_to_bytes` for any hashed byte (its layout is an engine serialisation detail, **[UNV]**, and not a stable cross-version canonical format). The tables are kept id-sorted by the mutators (BDY-9), so `snapshot()` verifies sortedness in debug and sorts only a table a defective caller left unsorted. (4) *No float state, no wall clock, no RNG* in the block or the hook; `Vector2i` may exist in memory, but the snapshot stores plain int arrays and `odometer` is never placed in a `Vector2i` (Body's own lint; SE-34's "no `Vector2i` in `snapshot()`" is the sibling precedent). (5) *Tick-source independence:* Body is correct for any number of `body.integrate` runs per rendered frame up to `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` 4; Presenters see only `pos_prev` and `pos_curr` of the last tick of a frame, and four catch-up ticks move at most 12 px, under `JUMP_CUT` (PIPE:501) at the default field. Body does not choose the tick source (kernel Open Question 2, KRN:957). (6) *Proofs:* PC-18 test 9 (replay identity) and the invariance fixture of BDY-2. *Decides:* KRN CR-13, D.12; R13. 211	**BDY-33 — The PROJECTOR slot.** Body registers exactly one `PROJECTOR` subscriber, `body.projector`, which owns (a) one per-body root `Node2D` per live `body_id` and its canvas TRANSLATION (rotation 0 by BDY-26; the avatar's body at the origin, others at BDY-27's offset); (b) the loaded body's bounding rectangle, published as the camera-limits rectangle to the Pipeline's camera solver on weld, detach and load (PIPE:165 C8) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0009 sync: OQ-C; `body.projector` never writes `Camera2D.limit_*`; the solver is the only clamp and the primary variant has no `Camera2D`, ADR-0008 section 6.2; confirmed with ADR-0034)*; and (c) nothing physical — no shape, no collision, no `PhysicsServer2D` call in the MVP. A PROJECTOR "writes engine-side derived objects ... never writes blocks" (CR-10). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Y-sort ownership and Presenter parenting.** (d) Each body root owns exactly one child layer node with `y_sort_enabled = true` — the **actor/props layer** — created, owned and freed by `body.projector`; Layout's section nodes (floor, wall faces) are siblings of that layer under the same root, never inside it, so the Pipeline's tie rule (PIPE D.12: layer order decides equal keys, the actor layer drawing after the wall layer) is a property of two named nodes and not of insertion order. (e) **Sort-key convention:** a Presenter's node `position` is set by the Presenter (the Controller's) to the integer `(p.x, p.y)` of PIPE D.9 in its body's frame, so the Y-sort key of an actor is its `y_foot = p.y` (PIPE D.12), and a prop's key is the Pipeline's `sort_y`; nothing in Body writes a sort key or a `z_index`. (f) **Reparent on `BODY_TRANSFER`:** when the P5 batch of tick `T` carries `BODY_TRANSFER{weld | detach | pod}` for an actor, `body.projector` moves that actor's Presenter node into the destination body's actor/props layer in the same tick and before the frame that follows it renders, then the Presenter writes its position from `pos_curr` in the destination frame (the engine's global-transform-preserving reparent is NOT used; whether `Node.reparent` keeps local or global position is **[UNV]**, ADR-BODY-03); Presenters register their node with the projector (`attach_presenter(actor_id, node)`) so Body, not the Controller, owns the move — a must-repeat for the Controller's Presenter story (8.3). The draw-order criteria of AC-BDY-69 and AC-BDY-73 depend on (d) to (f); AC-BDY-92b tests the parent after a weld, a cut and a pod hop. Layout's PROJECTOR parents its section nodes under Body's root for that `body_id` (**ASK Layout**, additive: LY:354 names "a per-body `Node2D`" without an owner). Whether a weld reparents section nodes or rebuilds the body's scene is the weld-spike-measured choice shared with ADR-LAY-03; it lives in ADR-BODY-03, not in behaviour text, and Y-sort under reparent and the tie rule are **[UNV]** (a HIGH gap Layout already carries). The Camera is a top-level node, never a child of a body; `physics_interpolation` is OFF for all presentation and `tick_alpha` is the one interpolator (PIPE:119 rule 8; ADR-BODY-04). *Decides:* R20; KRN:198; PIPE:165. (auto: projector contains no physical call; spike: reparent versus rebuild)
212	
213	**BDY-34 — Diagnostics.** Body owns `PC_FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP` (PCI:650 attributes the assert to "a Layout projection"; LY:222 routed it here, and it can run only where the rectangle and the foot box are both visible, which is Body's sweep), `diag.actor_in_footprint` (PIPE:727), the event `BODY_TRANSFER{weld|detach|pod}` with old and new body ids and the frame delta (the Pipeline rebases by it on a weld or detach, PIPE C5, and records `diag.cut_reason = BODY_TRANSFER` only when it cuts *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; `PC_BODY_TRANSFER{detach|pod}` is the Controller-spelled counter of PCI:651, fed by this event), the defect counters of BDY-9, BDY-23, BDY-21 and BDY-16 (`BDY_ORPHAN_ACTOR`, `BDY_OCTANT_INVALID`, `BDY_VEFF_INVALID`, `BDY_SEAT_UNBOUND`, `BDY_WORLD_LIMIT`, `BDY_TRANSFER_NO_SECTION`, `BDY_PLAN_MISMATCH`, and *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* `BDY_TRAPPED_ACTOR`, and *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6)* `BDY_REBASE_ACTOR_IN_CAP`) and per-actor sweep cost (microseconds per `body.integrate` actor step, logged above `SWEEP_COST_LOG_MS`). `BDY_BLOCKED_TICKS` is NOT created: the Controller's `PC_BLOCKED_TICKS` is cited. Diagnostics live in the hook's diagnostics channel, never in the block, never in the hashed set. *Decides:* R16, D17. (auto)
214	
215	**BDY-35 — Units, rounding and zoom invariance, stated once.** Every Body length is base px and identical at every ladder step; no `k`, `s`, `field_h` or zoom value appears in this GDD outside this sentence (modelled on LY-3 (e)). Two rounding rules are kept apart and never mixed: **`trunc` toward zero** is the SUB-PIXEL rule (PCI:157 amendment 2, PCI:904), applied only to `sub_a / 256` in BDY-13; **FLOOR division** is the px-to-tile rule (LY-3 (f)), applied only where a pixel becomes a tile or a local coordinate (`section_at`, the broadphase, `room_at` inputs). Each is a single named static helper in `IntMath` (`src/shared/int_math.gd`), shared by Body, Layout and Emitter, so they cannot be confused; the function list and divisor guard are owned by ADR-0005 section 1.4 and 1.7, and ADR-0010 section 5.4 fixes only the path and the single annotated site *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0010 sync)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Float-free definitions.** `trunc_div(a, b)` is the ONE annotated (`@warning_ignore("integer_division")`) `/` site in `src/` (ADR-0010 SIM-05, PRJ-04): with both operands typed `int` and `b != 0` it is integer division truncating toward zero (truncation toward zero and signed `%` probed 2026-10-28 on the 4.7.2 editor binary, ADR-0010 P11; the release-export repeat is LINT-SPIKE-1), and it contains no float, no `int()`/`floor()` call and no `Variant`. `floor_div(a, b)` for `b > 0` is `trunc_div(a - posmod(a, b), b)`: the numerator is an exact multiple of `b` (`posmod` is non-negative for `b > 0`), so the division is exact and the truncating/flooring distinction cannot arise; for `b <= 0` it is a defect (assert in debug). The fixtures below (`floor_div(-1, 48) == -1`) and the lint of BDY-3 prove both; no other `/` on integers is allowed in `src/`. GDScript's integer `/` truncating toward zero was probed on the 4.7.2 editor binary (ADR-0010 P11; the release-export repeat is LINT-SPIKE-1), and the unit-test root still carries engine-semantics fixtures — `trunc(-181 / 256) == 0`, `trunc(-362 / 256) == -1`, `trunc(-768 / 256) == -3`, `floor_div(-1, 48) == -1` — evaluated through the same expression the step uses; if the engine disagrees, the failure is a spike finding and the step uses an explicit sign-split expression. Body-frame coordinates and `offset_px` may be negative after a detach re-base (a negative-coordinate test is in Acceptance). *Decides:* R24; reflexion pattern 5. (auto + lint)

360	### D.1 Axis step
361	
362	The axis step formula is defined as:
363	
364	`sub_a += UNIT[o].a * v_eff;  step_a = trunc(sub_a / 256);  sub_a -= step_a * 256;  moved_a = sweep_a(step_a)`   (axis `a` in {x, y}, x first then y; the position advances by `moved_a`)
365	
366	This is PCI D.3's expression verbatim (PCI:275), re-sourced to this GDD. Both axes' residues advance BEFORE either sweep (BDY-9), so a refused x step never changes `sub_y`, and a refused step stores no energy and loses none.
367	
368	**Variables:**
369	
370	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
371	|---|---|---|---|---|
372	| `o` | int | 0 to 7 (the move octant of D.14; NONE never reaches this step) | `controller.state.octant`, or Body's own `last_octant` in the provisional decel ladder (D.14) | movement direction |
373	| `v_eff` | int | 0 to 3 (clamped into `[0, 3]` for the tick, BDY-9) | `controller.state` `gait_effective` (PCI D.4) | whole base px per tick requested this tick: `V_WALK`, `V_RUN` or `V_CARRY` as the Controller resolves it |
374	| `UNIT[o].a` | int | {-256, -181, 0, 181, 256} | the `UNIT` table of PCI D.3 (256 cardinal, 181 diagonal; cited, not restated) | per-axis velocity scale in 1/256 px |
375	| `sub_a` | int | -255 to 255 | `body.state` `actors[].sub` (persisted) | sub-pixel accumulator for axis `a`, 1/256 px |
376	| `step_a` | int | -3 to 3 | calculated | whole px requested on axis `a` before collision |
377	| `moved_a` | int | -3 to 3, `abs(moved_a) <= abs(step_a)` | calculated by the sweep (BDY-15) | whole px actually moved after the 1-px sweep against Layout's `solid_in` set |
378	
379	**Output Range:** `abs(step_a) <= 3` per tick. Cardinal motion leaves `sub` at 0 on every tick (`step = v_eff`). A diagonal tick moves `(k, k)` in magnitude, so a diagonal is always exactly 45 degrees; over 256 consecutive ticks in one octant the per-axis displacement is exactly `181 * v_eff` px for a diagonal and exactly `v_eff` px per tick for a cardinal, with `sub` returning to 0. `trunc` (not `floor`) is mandatory so that west mirrors east. `odometer += (abs(moved_x) + abs(moved_y)) * ODO_W[move octant]` after collision (`ODO_W` 256 cardinal, 181 diagonal; PCI:491), so a wall adds 0 and a diagonal slide `moved = (0, -1)` adds 181.
380	
381	**Example:** NE walk at `v_eff` 2 from `sub = (0, 0)`: the increment is `181 * 2 = 362` per axis per tick. `sub.x` runs 362 (step 1, residue 106), 468 (step 1, residue 212), 574 (step 2, residue 62), 424 (step 1, residue 168), 530 (step 2, residue 18), 380 (step 1, residue 124), 486 (step 1, residue 230), 592 (step 2, residue 80): steps **1, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 1, 2**, the cadence printed in PCI D.3. West mirror: NW at `v_eff` 1 from rest: tick 1 `sub.x = -181`, `step = trunc(-181 / 256) = 0`; tick 2 `sub.x = -362`, `step = -1`, residue `-362 + 256 = -106`; the east twin reads `(0, 181)` then `(1, 106)`, an exact mirror (a `floor` step would read `-1` and `+75` on tick 1).
382	
383	### D.2 Foot box

601	### D.12 Sweep cost bound
602	
603	The sweep cost bound formula is defined as:
604	
605	`swept(pos, step) = [pos.x - 8 + min(0, step_x), pos.x + 8 + max(0, step_x)) x [pos.y + min(0, step_y), pos.y + 8 + max(0, step_y));     cells <= 4;     tests <= 7 * K  (1-px loop: K for the exemption scan plus (abs(step_x) + abs(step_y)) <= 6 sub-steps times K);     T_actor = c_q + tests * c_r + c_commit`
606	
607	The swept box is the Minkowski cover of the foot box over the x-then-y path and is the ONE `solid_in` query of an actor-tick (BDY-15). A stationary actor issues no query and no sweep (BDY-9). An analytic clamp against each rectangle's near edge is permitted if and only if it is result-identical (an equivalence property test carries the proof; ADR-BODY-01) and reduces `tests` to about `3 * K`.
608	
609	**Variables:**
610	
611	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
612	|---|---|---|---|---|
613	| `step_x`, `step_y` | int | -3 to 3 | D.1 | whole px requested this tick |
614	| swept box width and height | int | `16 + abs(step_x)` (16 to 19) by `8 + abs(step_y)` (8 to 11) | calculated | at most 19 by 11 cells |
615	| `cells` | int | 1 to 4 | calculated; `BROADPHASE_CELL_PX` (Layout, LY:228) | a 19-px span crosses at most 2 broadphase cells per axis *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: this holds only while `BROADPHASE_CELL_PX >= FOOT_BOX_W + 3`, since the swept width is at most `FOOT_BOX_W + 3`; with `FOOT_BOX_W` 24 and a 24-px cell a swept box could touch 3 cells per axis and the 4-cell bound would break; Tuning Knobs)* |
616	| `K` | int | 0 to the densest 4 cells, far below `MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY` 2,000 | Layout's `solid_in` result | rectangles returned for this actor-tick |
617	| `c_q`, `c_r`, `c_commit` | microseconds | **[UNV]**, spike S1 metrics | measured | one broadphase query, one box-versus-rectangle test, one commit with dirty marking |
618	| `B` | microseconds | 50 | cited: PCI:1078 (0.05 ms per actor at P99, 4 actors 0.2 ms, against a body of `MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY` rectangles) | the per-actor budget; Body adds no figure |
619	
620	**Output Range:** at most 7 tests per returned rectangle for the literal 1-px loop, one `solid_in` call, at most 4 broadphase cells; the cost is bounded independently of the 2,000-rectangle worst case because the query returns only the swept cells' rectangles. Whether PCI:1078's 0.05 ms includes the `solid_in` call is not stated there; this GDD states that the budget covers query, sweep and commit (Open Question for the Controller owner to confirm).
621	
622	**Example:** `pos = (200, 140)`, `step = (0, -3)`: swept box `[192, 208) x [137, 148)`, 16 by 11 cells. With `K = 16`: the literal loop costs at most `7 * 16 = 112` tests, the analytic clamp about 48. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **No arithmetic is offered as evidence.** Every constant is **[UNV]** until spike S1, and the earlier illustration (`c_q + c_commit = 15 us`, `c_r = 0.25 us`, `T_actor = 43 us <= B`) used a native-code-scale `c_r`; interpreted GDScript is unlikely to be that fast, so `T_actor <= B` is spike S1's to settle and is not assumed here. The cited budgets, restated against the right denominators: eight actors (`MAX_ACTORS`) at the cited 0.05 ms are 0.4 ms, 20 % of the kernel's 2 ms P3 target; four actors at the cited 0.2 ms are 10 %. `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4 is only a logging threshold and is not the denominator.
623	
624	*(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **What the model above leaves out, and the whole-hook budget.** The figures above price only the moving-actor path, with the literal stepper, and the `c_r` 0.25 us of the earlier example was an **unmeasured illustration** (struck in the example above) (every constant is **[UNV]** until spike S1; it is not a design figure and no criterion gates on it). The full model, with the analytic clamp as the baseline (BDY-15) and the stepper only as the test oracle:
625	
626	`T_move = c_q + K * c_r * 3 + c_commit`   (ordinary moving actor, clamp against each returned rectangle's near edge, about `3 * K` tests)
627	`T_exempt = c_q + K * c_r + n_sub * (|E| * c_ov + c_sec) + c_commit`   (exempt actor, `n_sub <= abs(step_x) + abs(step_y) <= 6` candidate sub-steps, `c_ov` one per-rectangle overlap area, `c_sec` one `section_at` call for the exit-containment test, BDY-29)
628	`T_idle = c_commit`   (stationary: residue update and commit, no query)
629	`T_hook = n_bodies_moving * c_pose + sum over actors of (T_move | T_exempt | T_idle) + c_diag`
630	
631	Worst-case fixtures, committed with the criterion (AC-BDY-68): (W1) 8 actors all moving against the K = 16 cluster; (W2) 8 actors all EXEMPT at the abutting-pair cap with `|E| = 2`, all pressing east so every tick evaluates `E` and calls `section_at` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: W2 is NOT the most expensive exempt case; east is refused at the first candidate sub-step there, so `n_sub` = 1 and each actor pays one `|E| * c_ov + c_sec`)*; *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (W2b) 8 actors all EXEMPT inside F7's single 24 x 96 rectangle (a box wholly inside one rectangle, `|E| = 1`, the section-set stub answering a section for every candidate origin), octant 1 at `v_eff` 3, so every candidate sub-step is admitted and `n_sub` reaches its bound of 6: `T_exempt = c_q + K * c_r + 6 * (c_ov + c_sec) + c_commit` per actor, the most expensive exempt tick; (W2c) the mixed fixture, 4 moving actors (W1's K = 16 cluster), 2 exempt actors (W2b) and 2 idle actors, the realistic bound on a busy tick; (W3) 8 bodies all with `vel != 0` and 8 idle actors (pose step plus 8 commits); (W4) Suit's reads, 8 seats each calling `actor_section` and `actor_local_px` once per tick for `suit.vitals` (BDY-29: 8 `section_at` calls per tick from the consumer and none from the hook itself), added to the hook total of W1 and of W2b; (W5) a weld or cut tick, the detection event of BDY-16 for every actor on the touched bodies with the trapped-actor probe for each actor whose start box has `E` non-empty: `T_event = n_touched * c_q + n_flagged * 192 * (|E| * c_ov + c_sec)` (192 = 4 directions x `TILE_PX` 48), at most 8 x 192 = 1,536 overlap tests and 1,536 `section_at` calls, once per event and never per tick. **Separate bounds for moving and exempt actors *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*:** a moving actor costs at most `3 * K` box-versus-rectangle tests; an exempt actor costs at most `K` rectangle tests plus `n_sub * |E|` overlap evaluations plus `n_sub` `section_at` calls (`n_sub <= 6`), a different shape that `3 * K` does not describe (AC-BDY-117 gates each on its own count). **Catch-up worst frame:** a late frame runs `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` = 4 ticks (BDY-32), so the worst frame cost is `4 * T_hook` of the more expensive of W2b and W2c, plus W4; on the cited per-actor figure the arithmetic for 8 actors is `4 * 0.4 ms = 1.6 ms`, 27 % of `FRAME_SIM_BUDGET_MS` 6.0 (the budget of a frame that runs `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` ticks; a one-tick frame is 4.0), an upper bound on the cited figure only, to be replaced by the S1 measurement *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: was stated as 40 % of `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4, the wrong denominator)*. **Spike S1 is a hard prerequisite** of closing the Body hook story *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R12)*: every wall-clock figure in this section is gated on the two reference machines of delegated ruling R12 and is *pending spike measurement on RM-DESKTOP / RM-DECK*. **RM-DESKTOP** is the minimum-spec desktop: Windows 10/11 64-bit; a 6-core/6-thread CPU of the Intel Core i5-9400F / AMD Ryzen 5 2600 class; 8 GB RAM; a GPU of the NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti 4 GB / AMD Radeon RX 570 4 GB class (Vulkan 1.2+); SATA SSD; 1920x1080 at 60 Hz; P99 CPU frame-time ceiling 16.6 ms. **RM-DECK** is the handheld: Steam Deck LCD (2022), SteamOS stable, 1280x800 at 60 Hz panel, 30 fps target, P99 CPU frame-time ceiling 33.3 ms. **Build type for every wall-clock figure:** a release export (Godot 4.7.2 release export template, not the editor and not a debug template), renderer `forward_plus`, vsync on, the pipeline's 120-frame warm-up, with the startup read-back (renderer, driver) recorded with each result. **P99 headroom:** pass needs P99 <= 90 % of the ceiling (at least 1.7 ms of headroom on RM-DESKTOP, at least 3.3 ms on RM-DECK). The developer's machine is not a reference machine and its figures are indicative only (`project.yaml` `qa.min_spec`). Until S1 has recorded a number on both machines no figure in this section is a gate; the S1 baseline then becomes the +25 % reference (AC-BDY-117 (b)). The `STEP_BUDGET_MS` check is the logged share of the whole hook, not of one actor.

1	# ADR-0013: Ship Layout Block, Geometry and ID Allocation
2	
3	## Status
4	Proposed
5	
6	## Date
7	2026-10-29
8	
9	## Last Verified
10	2026-10-29 (against `design/gdd/ship-section-and-layout-data-model.md` LY-1 to LY-35 and D.5, D.6, D.9, D.10, D.12, D.21; ADR-0001 to ADR-0010, all Proposed; the engine facts marked "probed 2026-10-29" were run on the 4.7.2 mono console binary)
11	
12	## Decision Makers
13	Claude (author), running under modes.automation: autonomous (project.yaml); decisions logged for the user's review; the user has not yet reviewed this ADR.
14	
15	## Summary
16	Ship Section & Layout is the one owner of rooms, rectangles, sockets, welds, bodies and three id spaces, and every Core and Feature system reads or calls it, but no document fixes how its block is shaped, how its rectangles are keyed, how a weld moves a body or which side of the Layout/Graph boundary allocates which id. This ADR decides: `layout.state` stores **instances by reference** to immutable catalog templates as **dense per-column packed arrays** (rows addressed by `id - 1`, tombstones kept, a third persisted `structure_hash` added to the GDD's two); geometry is **integer half-open rectangles** with a flags byte in a reserved, never-renumbered `idx` space; sockets are **sparse terminal-state rows** changed only inside two mutators; weld offsets are computed on the **lower-`body_id` survivor** with a canonicalised `welds[]`; and ids are **split** so that Layout allocates `section_id`, `body_id` and `room_id` from persisted counters while the Graph allocates node, edge, compartment and seam ids and Layout only stores the per-instance bases.
17	
18	## Engine Compatibility
19	
20	| Field | Value |
21	|-------|-------|
22	| **Engine** | Godot 4.7.2 (pinned 4.7; installed 4.7.2.stable.mono, `docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md`) |
23	| **Domain** | Core (simulation data model; scene-tree free, integer-only; the PROJECTOR that draws it is ADR-0034's) |
24	| **Knowledge Risk** | MEDIUM. The module uses no rendering, physics or scene API. The two HIGH items it touches are the 4.7 packed-array element-write change (every dirty mark here is explicit inside a mutator) and the 4.7 typed-return override rule (it applies to the `@abstract` port of § 8; the rule is sourced from `breaking-changes.md` § 4.6 to 4.7) |
25	| **References Consulted** | `docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md`; `breaking-changes.md` (4.6 to 4.7 GDScript rows, 4.3 `TileMapLayer` row); `deprecated-apis.md`; `current-best-practices.md` § GDScript (4.7). **`docs/engine-reference/godot/modules/` has no core, scripting or tilemap file** (it holds animation, audio, input, navigation, networking, physics, rendering and ui), so every claim about `Array[String]` encoding, packed-array methods and GDScript cost below is either probed or marked UNVERIFIED. Project ADRs: 0001 to 0010 (§ Related) |
26	| **Post-Cutoff APIs Used** | Packed-array element writes that skip the property setter (4.7); `@abstract` ports (4.5, chosen by ADR-0010) for `LayoutGraphPort`; typed `Array[String]` as a persisted column. No `TileMapLayer`, `Node` or `Resource` API is used by this ADR |
27	| **Verification Required** | **V1 (probed 2026-10-29, done):** `PackedInt32Array.bsearch(v)` returns the insertion index and, for ties, the first index with `before = true` and one past the last with `before = false`; `PackedInt32Array.insert` and `remove_at` keep order; a value `0xDEADBEEF` stored in a `PackedInt32Array` reads back as `-559038737` and masks to `3735928559`; `var_to_bytes` then `bytes_to_var` returns a typed `Array[String]` still typed and a `PackedInt64Array` exact to 2^40; `PackedStringArray` also round-trips (but ADR-0006 § 1.2 does not allow it in a save, so it is not used); `duplicate()` of a packed array is independent of later element writes. **V2 (UNVERIFIED, spike S1 / SP-ENG-1):** the GDScript cost of the `layout.doors` loop at `MAX_DOORS_LOADED` doors on a release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK against its 0.2 ms line (TR-section-042). **V3 (UNVERIFIED, S1 with ADR-0014):** the P2 cost of `attach_section` and `detach_section` including the per-body broadphase rebuild at `MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY`. **V4 (UNVERIFIED, after ADR-0005 is Accepted):** golden vectors for `geometry_hash`, `visual_hash` and `structure_hash` of the four MVP templates, equal on the editor and on the `template_release` export (ADR-0007 CONTENT-EXP-1). **V5 (UNVERIFIED):** `Array[String]` column cost in `snapshot()` and in the type walk for the largest long-campaign shape of § 12 (tens of rows; expected negligible, measured in SAVE-WRK-1 f) |
28	
29	## ADR Dependencies
30	
31	| Field | Value |
32	|-------|-------|
33	| **Depends On** | ADR-0003 (block descriptor, Class A/B mutators, `WriteScope`, fault domains, owner-callable contract); ADR-0004 (dirty-key layout and `KeySpaceDescriptor`); ADR-0005 (canonical encoding, `Hash64.of_value`, `IntMath`, `low32`, block hash cache); ADR-0006 (snapshot types allowed in a save, two-phase `restore`, `ctx.fault`); ADR-0007 (template catalog, manifests, `section_templates` ledger, boot tiers); ADR-0010 (`src/sim/layout/`, ports, lint tiers, `## @hot`); ADR-0001 and ADR-0002 (P2/P3 phases, hook registration, no Layout command). None is Accepted yet, so this ADR cannot be Accepted before them |
34	| **Enables** | ADR-0014 (rect set, broadphase, `OccluderSource`), ADR-0015 (Body consumes `frame_shift`, `moved_sections`, `rects[]`, `section_at`), ADR-0016 (restore order and verifiers over this block), ADR-0017 (Emitter reads `version`/`static_version`, `anchor_geometry`), ADR-0021 (the weld transaction calls LM2/LM3), ADR-0026 (`init_world` calls LM1), ADR-0034 (PROJECTOR inputs and `entity_id` fields), ADR-0020, ADR-0023, ADR-0027 (read views) |
35	| **Blocks** | The Layout epic (template compile and hashes, `layout.state`, LM1 to LM4, `layout.doors`, read views); every Feature story that calls `build_section`, `attach_section`, `detach_section` or reads `rects_in`/`room_at`/`door_passage` |
36	| **Ordering Note** | Wave A. ADR-0011 (Graph data model, same wave) must supply the Graph side of § 3 and § 8: the `instantiate_section` return and its contiguity guarantees, the allocation-free `opening` read and the `LayoutGraphPort` implementation (§ Related lists every assumption). ADR-0014, ADR-0015, ADR-0016 and ADR-0034 are written afterwards and build on the records fixed here. Where this ADR and the Layout GDD differ (§ Related, "GDD sync"), the ADR is the proposal and the GDD is updated to it, not the reverse |
